subject: MSA + Order Form: proposed security-incident sub-limit and incorporation of Security Addendum
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Harrison Cole <hcole@palletlaw.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + Order Form: proposed security-incident sub-limit and incorporation of Security Addendum

Harrison,

Thanks for taking a look at the MSA and Order Form. We traced a couple of outstanding redline items and highlighted one key commercial/legal ask from the customer side: they want clarity that security incidents are carved out from the general contractual liability cap, and that a specific sub-limit apply to data-security incidents.

Our recommended language is: a dedicated security incident sub-limit of $2,000,000 for direct remediation costs and regulatory fines, which sits outside the overall contractual cap for general liabilities. We also want an explicit cross-reference to the Security Addendum so it is incorporated by reference (SOC2 evidence, notification timelines, and incident response obligations live there). Finally, Redwood prefers a standard consequential damages exclusion retained.

I attach the redlines and a short summary. Can you review whether:
- the proposed sub-limit wording is enforceable as drafted (i.e., separate pool vs. carve-out),
- referencing the Security Addendum is sufficient, or we need a defined term and a specific section pointer, and
- any insurer coordination language is advisable (carrier subrogation / coverage matters).

Next steps: if we get GC feedback this week, sales ops can push an updated countersigned Order Form and we can route the MSA for legal sign-off.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlines-msav2.docx (docx), breach-sublimit-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Harrison Cole <hcole@palletlaw.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Tara Simmons <tara.simmons@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-16T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: proposed security-incident sub-limit and incorporation of Security Addendum

Jordan / team,

Thanks — reviewed the redlines. High level thoughts:

1) Sublimit construct: carving security incidents out of the general cap is workable but important to clearly define the scope of incidents covered ("Security Incident" defined by the Security Addendum with examples: unauthorized access, exfiltration, ransomware). Without a tight definition, the sub-limit can be read broadly.

2) Dollar amount: our client prefers a compromise number; they are reluctant to accept a full $2M outside the cap. We proposed $1.5M as a starting point in markup and included alternative text that ties the sub-limit to insurer limits (i.e., recoveries limited to insured amounts first).

3) Fines and penalties: regulatory fines (e.g., GDPR/CCPA) should be expressly included in the sub-limit, subject to any non-waivable statutes. Consider adding language that requires cooperation with claimant to reasonably mitigate fines.

4) Incorporation: referencing the Security Addendum by section is stronger. Suggest: "Security Addendum, Section 2 (Definitions) and Section 4 (Incident Response & Remedies), is incorporated by reference."

5) Carve-outs we cannot accept: unlimited carve-out for intentional wrongdoing or gross negligence — those remain outside typical caps but need clear standard of proof.

I attached redline with inline comments. Happy to discuss on a short call.

-Harrison
Pallet Law (Outside Counsel)

Attachments: acme_redlines_msav1.docx (docx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: proposed security-incident sub-limit and incorporation of Security Addendum

Team,

Quick internal alignment:
- I prefer to keep the sub-limit explicit but lower than $2M given the customer's posture. If we can land at $1.75M and secure explicit incorporation of the Security Addendum, that will be an acceptable commercial compromise.
- We should keep regulatory fines and direct remediation costs inside the sub-limit; exclude consequential and speculative damages.
- On insurer coordination: include a clause that requires parties to reasonably cooperate with insurance claims but does not shift coverage obligations. No assignment of recovery to the customer.

Action items: Jordan please confirm whether sales will accept $1.75M as a counter if Harrison's mark lands at $1.5M. Neha, can you prepare a one-page fallback that enumerates negotiation bullets for the CS/sales pitch sheet? I'll schedule a 30-min sync with Harrison if needed.

—Laura
VP, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Laura / Jordan —

I drafted the fallback bullets for commercial to use with the customer. Summary below (send as one-pager with the Order Form):

• Redwood proposes a Security Incident Sublimit of $1,750,000 for direct remediation and regulatory liabilities; this amount is separate from and in addition to the general liability cap in Section 9.
• Security Addendum will be explicitly incorporated: reference Section 2 (Definitions) and Section 4 (Incident Response & Remedies).
• Consequential damages remain excluded across the agreement.
• Explicit cooperation clause for insurance claims; no requirement to assign proceeds to the customer.
• Carve-out for gross negligence and willful misconduct remains, but require clear definitions and high proof threshold.

If Harrison can live with 1.75M and incorporation language, we can present that as Redwood's final commercial position and ask the customer to accept via DocuSign. I added the bullets into a PDF and attached to this email.

-Neha
